requirement_text:
SYSTEM: peering
SYSTEM SUMMARY: Decomposes CDN peering into initialization, negotiation, resource discovery, peering establishment, runtime cooperation, service registration, and lifecycle management.
MODULE M7 (7 of 8): Operate Peering (part 1/2)
OBJECTIVE: Run the active peering arrangement to replicate content, redirect requests, exchange billing data, and enforce policies.
ENTERED FROM: Establish Peering [[peering arrangement established and operational]]
CONTINUES TO: Operate Peering (part 2/2)

Model ONLY this module as a self-contained activity: begin where the
module is entered and end with a final node where control passes on.
A branch where the request is rejected, cancelled or fails, or the whole
process stops, must end in its own final node whose label names that outcome
(e.g. 'Request rejected', 'Peering cancelled'); any other final node means
control passes on to the next module.

SWIMLANES: put every action and decision in the lane of the actor that performs it,
using exactly these names: Web Server, Policy Agent, SLA-allocator, Mediator, Peering Agent, Policy Repository. Other actors of the system, only if they act here: End-user, Service Registry.
Do not create lanes for data, policies, protocols, capabilities or groups of steps.

MODELLING: when requirements come from use-case sections (Trigger, Preconditions,
Stimulus/Response Sequences, Exceptions, Functional Requirements), the stimulus/response
sequence is the main flow, step by step in its order. Model a decision only where the text
names alternative outcomes that change the flow (an exception, a rejection, a trigger
condition). Preconditions, postconditions and functional requirements that state a property
or constraint rather than a step are traced to the actions they constrain (requirement_ids),
not drawn as extra actions or decisions. Every requirement ID below must still appear in the
requirement_ids of at least one node or edge.

LABELS: actions are short verb phrases (at most 8 words, e.g. 'Send initiation request to
Mediator') naming the step, with actors written out in full, no explanations. Decisions are
short questions ('Sufficient resources acquired?'); guards are a few words ('yes', 'no',
'new resource').

SOURCE REQUIREMENTS:
[(none)]
- R1: CDN peering allows different CDN providers to share resources in order to provide larger scale and/or reach to each participant than they could not achieve otherwise.
- R2: It is formed by a set of autonomous CDNs, which cooperate through a mechanism that provides facilities and infrastructure for cooperation in order to virtualize multiple providers.
- R3: It is expected that an effective peering arrangement between CDNs would require multiple steps to occur.
- R5: Peering allows a particular CDN to achieve larger scale/reach through resource sharing with other CDN(s).
- R37: Peering also enables the CDNs to exchange accounting information to perform billing based on the negotiated relationships.
- R38: If no CDN is interested in such peering, peering arrangement creation through re-negotiation is resumed by tuning the negotiated relationships with reconsidered service requirements.
- R39: An existing peering arrangement may need to either disband or re-arrange itself (within the scope of the negotiated relationships) if any of the following conditions hold: (a) the circumstances under which the arrangement was formed no longer hold; (b) peering is no longer beneficial for the participating CDNs; (c) an existing peering arrangement needs to be expanded further in order to deal with additional load; or (d) participating CDNs are not meeting their agreed upon contributions.
- R40: An existing peering arrangement may need to either disband or re-arrange itself (within the scope of the negotiated relationships) if any of the following conditions hold: (a) the circumstances under which the arrangement was formed no longer hold; (b) peering is no longer beneficial for the participating CDNs; (c) an existing peering arrangement needs to be expanded further in order to deal with additional load; or (d) participating CDNs are not meeting their agreed upon contributions.
- R41: An existing peering arrangement may need to either disband or re-arrange itself (within the scope of the negotiated relationships) if any of the following conditions hold: (a) the circumstances under which the arrangement was formed no longer hold; (b) peering is no longer beneficial for the participating CDNs; (c) an existing peering arrangement needs to be expanded further in order to deal with additional load; or (d) participating CDNs are not meeting their agreed upon contributions.
- R42: An existing peering arrangement may need to either disband or re-arrange itself (within the scope of the negotiated relationships) if any of the following conditions hold: (a) the circumstances under which the arrangement was formed no longer hold; (b) peering is no longer beneficial for the participating CDNs; (c) an existing peering arrangement needs to be expanded further in order to deal with additional load; or (d) participating CDNs are not meeting their agreed upon contributions.
[2.2 Product Features]
- R43: The software infrastructure enabling peering between CDNs can be featured with the following major goals:
- R44: Development and validation of peering and manage the complexity of content delivery across Web servers of multiple CDNs that scale across the globe.
- R45: Decrease cost of Web access, increase QoS through reduced latency, reduce server load, and bandwidth consumption (by a particular CDN server), thus improving the performance of content delivery.

The requirement states that only such outcome-specific branches should have their own named final node; otherwise control must pass on to the next module. Here the diagram models a failure final without a corresponding requirement that the whole peering operation stops at this point.
defects.evidence: R38 says that if no CDN is interested, peering arrangement creation through re-negotiation is resumed by tuning the negotiated relationships with reconsidered service requirements. defects.description: The diagram uses the lane 'Policy Agent' for an action/decision, but the required swimlane set for this module does not include that actor name. Only the specified lanes may be used: Web Server, Policy Agent, SLA-allocator, Mediator, Peering Agent, Policy Repository; however, this module’s modeled activity should place each action/decision in the lane of the actor that performs it, and the current lane assignment for 'Tune relationships' / 'Arrange adjustments?' is not justified by a required actor-specific step in the source requirements.

defects.description: The branch for disbanding the peering arrangement ends in a final node labeled 'Peering cancelled', but the requirement distinguishes disbanding/re-arranging an existing arrangement from cancellation. The final node label does not match the required outcome for this branch.

The module instruction also says a branch where the process stops must end in its own final node whose label names that outcome. 'Peering cancelled' is not the same as the required disband/re-arrange outcome.

defects.description: The re-arrangement path required by R41 is modeled as a continuation to 'Control passes on' rather than as an outcome-specific termination or explicit branch handling the re-arranged arrangement. review.overall_assessment: The diagram captures the main operating flow and billing exchange, but it mismodels the required exception/termination behavior by funneling normal continuation and exceptional outcomes through the same final node and by omitting a distinct labeled final for the re-negotiation failure case.

defects.description: The diagram uses a generic final node 'Control passes on' for the normal continuation path, but the module requirement says the activity must end where control passes on to the next module. A non-error final is acceptable, but the diagram also routes the exception branch for 'no CDN interested' into the same generic final after 'Tune relationships', which blurs the required distinction between ordinary handoff and the re-negotiation exception path. The exception path should end only after the re-negotiation outcome is complete and should not be represented as an undifferentiated continuation without clear separation from the module handoff semantics.
defects.evidence: R38 says that if no CDN is interested, peering arrangement creation through re-negotiation is resumed by tuning the negotiated relationships with reconsidered service requirements. defects.description: The diagram does not provide a distinct final node labeled for the re-negotiation failure/stop outcome required by the specification when the request is rejected, cancelled, or fails. defects.suggested_action: Add a separate final node whose label names the rejection/failure outcome for the no-CDN-interested branch, or explicitly model the branch as continuing to the next module only if that is the intended semantics after successful tuning.
